text:
Jake DeBrusk is playing through a week of trade headlines. Reports from Daily Hive, Markerzone and others say teams are calling and that the Canucks are holding firm on their asking price, while Thomas Drance, per Vancouver Hockey Daily, sees a market problem for both DeBrusk and Brock Boeser. On a team that just lost seven straight, that talk isn't going away.

On the ice, he's doing his job and not getting paid for it. Six goals on 8.7 expected goals means he's getting the looks without the finish, and his rate of 1.49 expected goals per 60 minutes is one of the higher marks on the roster. Five of his 12 points have come on the power play. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 55% of his shots coming off the rush last season, so he's dangerous in the seconds after a turnover.

Context matters for his five-on-five numbers. Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 94th percentile last season and his teammates near the bottom. Vancouver still does seven points better with him on the ice than without. Goals tend to follow chances; whether they come in Vancouver is the open question.
headline: DeBrusk keeps shooting, through the trade talk
